definition: An equation that contains a derivative, such as $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = ky$; solving it means finding the function itself.

A method for solving $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = f(x)\,g(y)$ where $g(y) \neq 0$: rearrange to $\int \frac{1}{g(y)}\,\mathrm{d}y = \int f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$, then integrate both sides with one constant.
The solution of a differential equation written with arbitrary constants, one for a first-order equation and two for a second-order one, so that it describes a whole family of solution curves.

The one solution of a differential equation that also fits the given conditions, such as a known value at $t = 0$; the conditions fix the constants in the general solution, one condition for each constant.
